system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: As of August 2026, a father punishes his 8-year-old child by striking the child, leaving bruises on the leg, claiming it was for discipline. Under Section 1567(2) of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code as currently in force, does this fall within the scope of parental authority? Answer only "within scope" or "outside scope", quoting one phrase from the provision.
raw_response: **Outside scope** — quoting the amended Section 1567(2), which permits a parent to discipline a child only "in a reasonable manner for the purpose of upbringing, **which must not be an act constituting cruelty to the child's body or mind**" ("ต้องไม่เป็นการกระทำที่มีลักษณะเป็นการทารุณจิตใจหรือร่างกายของบุตร"). Striking the child hard enough to leave bruises falls squarely within this excluded category, so it is not protected under parental authority.
